mechanism_narrative: A continued lift in WORKPLACES mobility signals more commuting and midday trips, which expands discretionary stops and raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect should appear when WORKPLACES is flat-to-rising for at least two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean within the next 28 days after two consecutive weeks of stable or rising WORKPLACES mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT relative to its recent trough increases access to shopping and leisure corridors, pushing RETAIL_REC upward within one to two weeks. The signal is strongest when TRANSIT stops falling and turns up from one week to the next.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises week-on-week after being below -35 for at least 2 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean for the next 14 days even though TRANSIT rises week-on-week from a depressed level.

mechanism_narrative: Higher RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent at home, which substitutes away from retail outings and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks. This mechanism should persist when residential time remains elevated relative to baseline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week average over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above the current level.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility rises while RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated, households are likely reallocating leisure time toward local outdoor activity instead of retail visits, which suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. Either input alone is too weak; the combined leisure-at-home pattern is required.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL stays above 5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to its last-4-week mean within 14 days when PARKS increases and RESIDENTIAL remains above 5.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT below the recent norm signals renewed disruption or tighter movement constraints, which reduces access to shopping districts and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect should emerge after the transit decline persists for at least one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2 points below its prior week and stays below -37
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline below its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days after TRANSIT drops and stays below -37.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both improve together, routine daytime trip chains expand and spill over into nearby retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week to one month. This interaction is strongest when grocery trips are stable or rising and workplace mobility is also rising.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both rise for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean within 28 days after both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES rise for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained PARKS dip during the late-summer window indicates a shift away from outdoor leisure that redirects activity toward indoor commercial venues, supporting a modest rise in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The signal is seasonal and should not operate outside warm-weather weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week mean within 14 days while PARKS remains below its recent average in late-summer weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL falls while TRANSIT remains depressed, the likely cause is renewed out-of-home activity without full venue normalization, which can depress retail visits because trip patterns fragment across necessities rather than shopping. Under that regime, RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5 while TRANSIT stays below -37
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean within 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL dropping below 5 and TRANSIT staying below -37.
